jurisdiction.name: Mexico
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Mexico has no AI-specific federal law as of October 2026; dozens of AI bills and constitutional initiatives to give Congress power to legislate on AI are pending, and the Chamber of Deputies has passed deepfake reforms to the Federal Criminal Code and two general laws that await the Senate. The 2025 data protection laws give a right to object to automated decisions and require impact assessments in the public sector; oversight of private-sector data protection moved from the dissolved INAI to the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno, which has issued no AI guidance, so INAI's 2024 AI recommendations remain the main data-protection guidance on AI. Federal laws on intellectual property, copyright and labour (AI voice and image cloning), dispute resolution, platform work, public-security intelligence and missing persons contain AI or algorithm provisions. The Digital Transformation and Telecommunications Agency (ATDT, created 2024) published a National AI Plan in 2026, and the science ministry and ATDT issued the Principios de Chapultepec on AI ethics; the 2018 AI strategy and principles are historical. The electoral institute INE is the most active rule-maker, with internal AI guidelines and an AI-system register and rules on AI-generated images of minors in campaigns. Jalisco has a binding AI policy for its administration, several states have penal reforms on AI-generated intimate content, and Monterrey has AI principles in its technology governance regulation.
lead_institutions: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones
Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 11 October 2026, covering federal laws, regulations and bills, federal ministries, regulators, ten states and the cities of Guadalajara, Monterrey, Mérida and San Pedro Garza García. Searches were made in Spanish and English. Some official websites could not be read automatically, including the National AI Plan file on the digital agency's portal, parts of the Mexico City, Querétaro and Estado de México gazettes and the banking regulator's compiled rules; records from those sites are marked as located but not fully read, or held as pending. Bills, including the federal AI law proposals, are listed as pending rather than as instruments. Pending: federal AI legislation, the deepfake reforms awaiting the Senate, the digital agency's promised guidelines for public-sector AI, the Querétaro judiciary's AI guidelines, and the states of Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, Baja California and Veracruz.

instruments.english_title: Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión; promulgated by the Presidencia de la República
instruments.publisher_name: Congreso de la Unión
instruments.current_status: Issued as Artículo Tercero of the decree published in the DOF on 20 March 2025, in force the next day (Transitorio Primero); abrogated the 2010 LFPDPPP (DOF 5 July 2010). Last amended DOF 14 November 2025 (art. 4, procedural harmonisation). The supervisory authority ('Secretaría') is the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno (art. 2 fr. XV); INAI's references and functions pass to the bodies that acquire them (Transitorio Cuarto). No AI-specific provision; the right to object covers automated processing.
instruments.scope: Private-sector data controllers and processors in Mexico
instruments.summary: Mexico's current private-sector data protection law, replacing the 2010 law and transferring supervision from the dissolved INAI to the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno. It governs the lawful processing of personal data, including for training and running AI systems, through principles, privacy notices and ARCO rights. Article 26 lets data subjects object to automated processing that produces unwanted legal effects or significantly affects them and that evaluates, without human intervention, aspects such as work performance, economic situation, health, reliability or behaviour.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection law governing AI processing of personal data, with a right to object to solely automated profiling; names INAI's successor authority.

instruments.summary: Mexico's first private-sector data protection law, issued by decree of 5 July 2010 that also reformed the federal transparency law to give the federal transparency institute (later INAI) data-protection powers. It set the principles of lawfulness, consent, notice, quality, purpose, loyalty, proportionality and accountability, ARCO rights and the verification and sanction procedures applied to private controllers. It was repealed by the decree of 20 March 2025 that issued the new LFPDPPP.

instruments.issuing_authority: Presidencia de la República (Felipe Calderón Hinojosa)
instruments.publisher_name: Diario Oficial de la Federación (Secretaría de Gobernación)

instruments.summary: Executive regulation of the 2010 private-sector data protection law, detailing consent, privacy notices, security measures, transfers, ARCO procedures and verification. Article 112 ('decisiones sin intervención humana valorativa') requires controllers that use personal data in a decision-making process without the assessment of a natural person to inform the data subject, who may use access and rectification rights to learn which data were used and seek reconsideration of the decision.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mexican federal legal instrument relevant to AI (data-privacy, transparency).

instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión (Cámara de Diputados and Senado de la República); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: Cámara de Diputados del H. Congreso de la Unión
instruments.current_status: In force since 21 March 2025 (transitorio Primero of the decree of 20 March 2025); last amended by the decree of 14 November 2025.
instruments.summary: General law governing personal data held by public authorities, bodies, parties and other 'sujetos obligados' at federal, state and municipal level, issued by the decree of 20 March 2025 that dissolved INAI's role: the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno and the 'Autoridades garantes' (internal-control bodies, INE for political parties and state counterparts) now oversee compliance. Article 41(II) lets data subjects object to automated processing without human intervention that evaluates or predicts personal aspects and produces unwanted legal or significant effects. Article 68 requires a data protection impact assessment, filed with the Secretaría or the competent Autoridad garante, before a public body puts into operation or modifies policies, IT systems, applications or other technologies involving intensive or relevant processing of personal data.

instruments.english_title: Decree amending the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States on organic simplification (extinction of INAI and other autonomous bodies)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión and state legislatures (Poder Revisor de la Constitución); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: Diario Oficial de la Federación (Secretaría de Gobernación)

instruments.summary: Constitutional reform that removes the autonomous transparency and data-protection guarantor (INAI) and other autonomous bodies from the Constitution. It rewrites Article 6 so that data protection in the public sector is guaranteed through internal-control and oversight bodies under a general law, assigns INE competence over political parties' data, and provides that the law referred to in Article 90 (the federal public administration law) determines the authority competent for verification and sanctions over personal data held by private parties. Transitorios give Congress 90 days to adapt the laws and end the INAI commissioners' functions when that legislation enters into force.

instruments.english_title: Decree amending the Organic Law of the Federal Public Administration (creation of the Agency for Digital Transformation and Telecommunications) — DOF 28 November 2024
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión (Cámara de Diputados and Senado de la República); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: Diario Oficial de la Federación (Secretaría de Gobernación)

instruments.summary: Reform of the Organic Law of the Federal Public Administration that adds the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (ATDT) to the centralised administration (art. 26) and sets its powers in a new Article 42 Ter: digital-government, ICT and telecommunications policy; guidelines on digital identity, interoperability, data analysis across federal agencies, open data and public software; information-security protocols for the federal administration; technological-sovereignty policy; and binding rules and technical opinions on federal ICT procurement. Transitorios transfer the resources and references of the Coordinación de Estrategia Digital Nacional to the ATDT. The text contains no AI-specific provision; it is the legal basis of the federal body that leads digital and AI policy for the administration.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mexican federal legal instrument relevant to AI (government-governance, public-sector, binding-law).

instruments.english_title: National Law to Eliminate Bureaucratic Procedures

instruments.summary: National law on administrative simplification and digitalisation that applies to federal, state and municipal authorities and replaces the Ley General de Mejora Regulatoria. It designates the ATDT as the National Simplification and Digitalisation Authority (art. 8) and creates a Modelo Nacional para la Digitalización (arts. 57-60): tools to remove discretion and corruption and speed up procedures through systematised and automated processes and digital platforms, with the CURP as the single identity key in all procedure registers and a preference for hosting data on the authorities' own infrastructure.

instruments.official_title: Decreto por el que se adicionan diversas disposiciones de la Ley Federal del Trabajo, en materia de Plataformas Digitales
instruments.english_title: Decree adding provisions to the Federal Labour Law on digital platforms (algorithmic management of platform work)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión (Cámara de Diputados and Senado de la República); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: Diario Oficial de la Federación (Secretaría de Gobernación)
instruments.current_status: Transitorio Primero: in force 180 days after publication in the DOF of 24 December 2024, i.e. 22 June 2025 (date computed from the transitorio; not stated as a calendar date in the decree).
instruments.summary: Adds a chapter on platform work to the Federal Labour Law. Article 291-J requires the rules for assigning tasks through algorithms to be transparent, clear and known to platform workers, defines an algorithm as the use of decision-making systems that exercise command and supervision over the worker in an automated or analogous way, and obliges platforms to draw up an algorithmic work-management policy in plain language explaining the elements algorithms use for decisions affecting the employment relationship (including access to future tasks, bonuses or sanctions). The algorithm must be reasonable, must not endanger workers' health or be a factor of discrimination.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mexican federal legal instrument relevant to AI (sectoral, transparency, binding-law).

instruments.official_title: Ley General de Mecanismos Alternativos de Solución de Controversias
instruments.english_title: General Law on Alternative Dispute Resolution Mechanisms
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión (Cámara de Diputados and Senado de la República); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: Diario Oficial de la Federación (Secretaría de Gobernación)
instruments.current_status: In force from 27 January 2024 (transitorio Primero of the decree of 26 January 2024).
instruments.summary: General law on mediation, conciliation and other alternative dispute resolution mechanisms, including a section on online dispute resolution (arts. 86-92). It defines 'sistemas automatizados' as software designed for tasks requiring artificial intelligence (machine learning, data processing, natural language processing, algorithms, neural networks) used for online dispute resolution, allows parties to agree to resolve disputes through automated or decentralised-justice systems, and sets the principles of full knowledge and 'transparencia algorítmica' (algorithms made visible, understandable and auditable). Parties have the right to know whether and how automated systems are used.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mexican federal legal instrument relevant to AI (transparency, sectoral, binding-law).

instruments.official_title: Decreto por el que se reforman y adicionan diversas disposiciones de la Ley Federal del Trabajo y de la Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor, en materia de derechos de las personas trabajadoras artistas intérpretes o ejecutantes
instruments.english_title: Decree amending the Federal Labour Law and the Federal Copyright Law on the rights of performing-artist workers (AI voice and image cloning)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión (Cámara de Diputados and Senado de la República); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.publisher_name: Diario Oficial de la Federación (Secretaría de Gobernación)
instruments.current_status: In force from 15 May 2026 (transitorio Primero). Transitorio Tercero requires the Copyright Law regulation to be amended within 60 days. Approved by the Cámara de Diputados on 7 April 2026 and the Senate on 15 April 2026 (Gaceta Parlamentaria).
instruments.summary: Amends the Federal Labour Law and the Federal Copyright Law to protect performers against AI. Labour contracts with performers must specify the conditions and pay for use of their image or voice through AI systems (LFT art. 305 Bis); under the Copyright Law, consent protection for a performer's image and voice extends to outputs generated by AI systems (art. 87), any AI cloning or impersonation of a performer's voice or image requires a prior written agreement (art. 121), and performers may oppose AI impersonation (art. 118, fr. VII) that clones their performances or simulates their voice identifiably, subject to parody, satire and creative-imitation exceptions. Article 102 now protects computer programs 'including those of artificial intelligence' as literary works.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mexican federal legal instrument relevant to AI (generative-ai, sectoral, binding-law).

instruments.publisher_name: Congreso de la Unión

instruments.scope: All persons subject to the LFPPI; enforced by the Instituto Mexicano de la Propiedad Industrial (IMPI)
instruments.summary: Broad reform of Mexico's industrial property law covering technology transfer, provisional patent applications, maximum resolution times for IMPI and other procedural simplifications. Of AI relevance, it adds a paragraph to article 386 providing that all the administrative infringements of industrial property rights listed there are also sanctioned when committed through the use of artificial intelligence, which IMPI investigates ex officio or on complaint and penalises with fines and closures under article 388.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with an explicit AI provision (AI-enabled IP infringements), enforced by IMPI.

instruments.english_title: Organic Law of the Mexican Navy (2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Unión (Cámara de Diputados and Senado de la República); promulgated by the President of the Republic

instruments.summary: New organic law of the Navy replacing the 2021 law. Among the Navy's powers (art. 2, XIX) are cyber-defence and cybersecurity activities and 'the use of artificial intelligence as a technological tool'; it establishes Strategic Support Units for Cyber-defence and Artificial Intelligence (arts. 5 and 37), operational units applying AI-based solutions as an analytical tool for operations in cyberspace, the electromagnetic spectrum, information operations and space, in support of naval operations.

instruments.official_title: Reglamento Interior de los Tribunales Agrarios
instruments.english_title: Internal Regulation of the Agrarian Courts (2024) — creates the Agrarian Artificial Intelligence System (SIAA)
instruments.issuing_authority: Tribunal Superior Agrario (Pleno)
instruments.publisher_name: Diario Oficial de la Federación (Secretaría de Gobernación)
instruments.current_status: In force from 29 June 2024 (transitorio Primero); abrogates the internal regulation of 8 January 2019. The DOF HTML page carries only the opening of the text; the full DOF pages are reproduced in the Cámara de Diputados PDF.
instruments.summary: Internal regulation of the federal agrarian courts approved by the Pleno of the Tribunal Superior Agrario on 4 June 2024. Its chapter on digital agrarian justice creates the Sistema de Inteligencia Artificial Agraria (SIAA, art. 181), a technological mechanism for managing agrarian case files whose use, capture and feeding is mandatory for all court staff; users must be trained, follow the manuals, keep credentials confidential, record entries on time and report anomalies, and the information is for the courts' exclusive use (arts. 182-183). Clerks, study secretaries and actuaries are each tasked with feeding the SIAA.

instruments.official_title: Plan Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Plan (April 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones
instruments.publisher_name: Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones
instruments.current_status: Cover dated 'Abril 2026'; the PDF is linked from the ATDT's 'Planes Nacionales 2030 – Inteligencia Artificial' page (upload path dated June 2026). A plan, not law: it proposes a future federal AI law and public-sector AI guidelines that had not been issued as of 11 October 2026. No DOF publication found.
instruments.scope: Federal government; sets the national AI agenda
instruments.summary: Mexico's first national AI plan, issued by the ATDT, built on three pillars: a sound ethical and legal framework; capabilities, talent and public software (the Centro Público de Formación en IA and a government 'Fábrica de IA'); and strategic infrastructure for technological sovereignty (the Coatlicue public supercomputer and data-centre investment). It adopts the Principios de Chapultepec as the ethical basis, commits to defining guidelines for responsible public-sector AI use, creating impact-assessment mechanisms and harmonising the regulatory framework, and proposes a federal AI law built on six principles (transparency and explainability, lawfulness and ethical use, non-discrimination, proportionality, effective human oversight, co-responsibility). It describes a governance model of strategic stewardship with distributed implementation in which the ATDT leads technical standards and guidelines, while supervisory, conformity-assessment and rights-protection functions are to be defined as the legal framework evolves.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mexican federal instrument shaping AI governance (strategy, government-governance, public-sector, ethics).

instruments.official_title: Principios de Chapultepec. Declaración de ética y buenas prácticas para el uso y desarrollo de la Inteligencia Artificial
instruments.english_title: Chapultepec Principles: Declaration of Ethics and Good Practices for the Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación (Secihti) and Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones (ATDT), jointly
instruments.publisher_name: Secretaría de Ciencia, Humanidades, Tecnología e Innovación
instruments.current_status: Presented and signed in Mexico City on 29 January 2026. The text states that its adoption has an orienting character ('carácter orientador'). A designed edition (February 2026) and a bilingual Spanish–English edition (May 2026) were later posted by Secihti. Cited by the April 2026 Plan Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial as the Government's first official AI ethics framework.
instruments.scope: Public policies, regulations and institutional instruments across the AI lifecycle; addressed to public institutions and other actors
instruments.summary: Joint Secihti–ATDT declaration setting ten guiding ethical principles for the design, use and development of AI in Mexico, intended to orient public policies, regulations and institutional instruments throughout the AI lifecycle. The principles include that AI must expand rights and never reduce them; every AI-supported decision must have accountable humans within clear institutional frameworks; a decision that cannot be explained must not be automated; social, territorial and environmental effects must be assessed before automating; and data are a public good to be protected. Other principles cover collective governance, public value, technological sovereignty, education and knowledge, cultural and linguistic diversity (including indigenous languages), and cybersecurity across the data lifecycle.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mexican federal instrument shaping AI governance (ethics, public-sector, government-governance).

instruments.official_title: Principios Generales para el desarrollo y uso de sistemas basados en Inteligencia Artificial en la Administración Pública Federal y Guía para análisis de impacto en el desarrollo y uso de sistemas basados en Inteligencia Artificial en la Administración Pública Federal (Versión 1.0)
instruments.english_title: General Principles for the Development and Use of AI-based Systems in the Federal Public Administration, and Impact Assessment Guide for AI-based Systems in the Federal Public Administration (Version 1.0)
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidencia de la República — Coordinación de Estrategia Digital Nacional, with the Unidad de Gobierno Digital of the Secretaría de la Función Pública and the Subcomisión de Inteligencia Artificial of the CIDGE
instruments.publisher_name: Presidencia de la República
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 published on gob.mx in a report compiling comments from the public consultation held 30 October – 18 November 2018 via gob.mx/participa; the document itself carries no publication date. Issued by bodies of the 2012–2018 administration (the Coordinación de Estrategia Digital Nacional and the Secretaría de la Función Pública no longer exist in that form); no official act adopting it as binding or withdrawing it was found, and the current administration's Principios de Chapultepec (2026) and Plan Nacional de IA (2026) do not refer to it. Kept as historical.
instruments.scope: Federal public administration (agencies developing or using AI systems)
instruments.summary: Report compiling the 51 comments received in the 2018 public consultation and setting out version 1.0 of the general principles and the impact-assessment guide for AI in the federal public administration. The principles are grouped under human rights, equity and social welfare, transparency, and responsibility and obligations. The guide, based mainly on Canada's Algorithmic Impact Assessment, scores five dimensions (data use and management, process, autonomy and functionality, reach on individuals/business/society, and reach on government operations) to classify a system at impact levels I–IV, and lists level-dependent requirements: registration with the SFP's Unidad de Gobierno Digital, reports on ethical risks, bias and robustness testing, external audits, human-in-the-loop, user notification, explanations and appeal mechanisms.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-11 in five parts (M1 federal law and bills; M2 federal government incl. ministry-level search per PROTOCOL §2; M3 regulators; M4 states, plus an M4b follow-up for Guanajuato; M5 cities). No usage-limit interruption; MEX had no earlier records. M1 full-text scanned the Cámara de Diputados portal (317 laws, 163 law regulations, 59 federal regulations) and 118 LXVI-legislature AI iniciativas; M3 screened 318 DOF notices containing 'inteligencia artificial' (2017-2026); M4b scanned 1,819 Guanajuato Periódico Oficial issues (2023-2026) via its public API and the Congress's 114 compiled laws (a missing intermediate certificate was added to a local CA bundle; verification stayed on). drafts: no consultation draft or anteproyecto on AI was found (bills are leads). standards: no NMX adoption of ISO/IEC AI standards found. sandbox: no AI regulatory sandbox found (Ley Fintech sandbox not AI-specific). index-readiness: no government-published AI readiness index (UNESCO RAM report not government-published). Located-only (2): National AI Plan (portal.atdt.gob.mx PDF 403 to curl and WebFetch; ATDT agenda page read); Estrategia IA-MX 2018 (live gob.mx page HTTP 500; text seen only in a web-archive capture, so not treated as read). LFPDPPP 2025 and the April 2026 LFPPI reform were found by M1 and M3 and are recorded once. www.dof.gob.mx fails the TLS name check; dof.gob.mx was used. Guanajuato: only Decreto Legislativo 184 (AI forensic matching database) has AI wording; no AI law or penal reform. Mérida's July 2026 council resolution (AI pilot with Chile) and San Pedro Garza García's AI secretariat are recorded as narrow local instruments.
